record.title: Unicity conjecture for the generalized Markov values m(c(n,d))
record.statement:
Let $c(n,d)$ be the path associated with $(n,d)$ in the generalized Markov construction, and let $m(c(n,d))$ denote its associated value. **Unicity conjecture.** If

$$
n\leq d,\qquad n'\leq d',\qquad m(c(n,d))=m(c(n',d')),
$$

then

$$
n=n'\quad\text{and}\quad d=d'.
$$

Thus, within the region $n\leq d$, the values $m(c(n,d))$ should determine the pair $(n,d)$ uniquely. The source presents this as a stronger conjecture motivated by the observed repetitions and does not provide a resolution in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Clément Lagisquet, Edita Pelantová, Sébastien Tavenas and Laurent Vuillon, “On the Markov numbers: fixed numerator, denominator, and sum conjectures”, arXiv:2010.10335 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.10335

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2020).

record.title: North Pole maximal directed discrepancy conjecture for Polar Coordinates
record.statement: Let $n\in\mathds{Z}^+$, and consider the point configuration called **Polar Coordinates with parameter $n$**. For a direction on the sphere, let the directed Discrepancy be the discrepancy measured in that direction. **North Pole maximal directed discrepancy conjecture.** Polar Coordinates with parameter $n$ has maximum directed Discrepancy in the direction of the North Pole. This conjecture asserts that the North Pole is a worst-case direction for the directional discrepancy of this highly symmetric point configuration; the paper proposes it based on observations and seeks evidence toward a proof.
record.source_name: Milad Bakhshizadeh, Ali Kamalinejad and Mina Latifi, “A practical algorithm to calculate Cap Discrepancy”, arXiv:2010.10454 (2020).

record.title: The extremal conjecture for $S_1$-free cyclic geometric hypergraphs
record.statement:
Let $\Omega_n$ be the vertices of a regular $n$-gon, and let $\operatorname{ex}_\circlearrowright(n,S_1)$ denote the maximum number of triangles in an $n$-vertex cyclic geometric hypergraph containing no copy of the configuration $S_1$. For $n\geq 5$, the conjectured extremal value is

**The $S_1$ extremal conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ex}_\circlearrowright(n,S_1)=\dot{\Delta}(n)+\left\lfloor\frac n2\right\rfloor\left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

The authors state more broadly that all extremal $S_1$-free cyclic geometric hypergraphs should belong to the previously defined family $\mathcal{H}^+(n)$. The exact value is not determined in the paper; only lower and upper bounds are proved, so this conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Zoltán Füredi, Dhruv Mubayi, Jason O'Neill and Jacques Verstraëte, “Extremal problems for pairs of triangles”, arXiv:2010.11100 (2020).

record.title: Eventual n-periodicity of maximum-independent-set counts
record.statement:
For positive integers $n$ and nonnegative integers $d$, let $G_n(d)$ be the graph whose vertices are the monomials of degree $d$ in $n$ variables, with two monomials adjacent exactly when their least common multiple has degree $d+1$. Let $\mathbf{a}_n(d)$ denote the number of maximum independent sets of $G_n(d)$. **Periodicity conjecture.** For any $n \geq 1$, there exists some $N \geq 0$ such that the sequence $\{\mathbf{a}_n(d)\}_{d \geq N}$ is $n$-periodic.

This is the paper's second conjecture concerning the eventual behavior of maximum-independent-set counts. It is posed alongside the conjecture on eventual uniqueness at degrees divisible by $n$; the supplied text gives no general proof or resolution.
record.source_name: John Machacek, “Unique maximum independent sets in graphs on monomials of a fixed degree”, arXiv:2010.11112 (2021).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1103.3309](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.3309).

record.title: Hat-guessing number bound for complete bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $K_{n,n}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $n$ vertices in each part, and let $\mathrm{HG}(G)$ denote the hat-guessing number of a graph $G$. For $n\geq 3$, the conjectured bound is

**Complete bipartite hat-guessing conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{HG}\left(K_{n,n}\right)\leq n.
$$

This generalizes the proved value $\mathrm{HG}\left(K_{3,3}\right)=3$ and would determine the upper bound suggested by the known inequality $\mathrm{HG}\left(K_{n,n}\right)\leq n+1$. The question remains open for $n>3$.
record.source_name: Xiaoyu He, Yuzu Ido and Benjamin Przybocki, “Hat Guessing on Books and Windmills”, arXiv:2010.13249 (2020).

record.title: Alspach–Mason–Pullman consistency conjecture for even-order tournaments
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tournament, let $d_T^+(v)$ and $d_T^-(v)$ denote the outdegree and indegree of $v$, and define its excess by

$$
\operatorname{ex}(T)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{v\in V(T)}\lvert d_T^+(v)-d_T^-(v)\rvert.
$$

A path decomposition of $T$ is a decomposition of its edges into directed paths, and $\operatorname{pn}(T)$ is the minimum number of paths in such a decomposition. **Alspach–Mason–Pullman's conjecture.** If $T$ has even order, then

$$
\operatorname{pn}(T)=\operatorname{ex}(T).
$$

The excess is a general lower bound for the path number, so the conjecture asserts that this bound is always sharp for even-order tournaments. The conjecture is known for sufficiently large even tournaments and for several large-excess cases, but the general statement remains open.
record.source_name: António Girão, Bertille Granet, Daniela Kühn, Allan Lo and Deryk Osthus, “Path decompositions of tournaments”, arXiv:2010.14158 (2022).

record.title: Best-bound conjecture for the star chromatic index of outerplanar graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an outerplanar graph with maximum degree $\Delta$. The **outerplanar star chromatic index conjecture.**

$$
\chi_{\mathrm{star}}'(G) \leq \lfloor 1.5\Delta \rfloor + 1.
$$

This would improve the known bound $\chi_{\mathrm{star}}'(G)\leq \lfloor 1.5\Delta\rfloor+5$ for outerplanar graphs and is presented as the conjectured best upper bound for the star chromatic index. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Xuling Hou, Lingxi Li and Tao Wang, “Star edge-coloring of some special graphs”, arXiv:2010.14349 (2020).

record.title: Quadratic universal graph conjecture for bipartite permutation graphs
record.statement:
For each positive integer $n$, let $U_n$ be a bipartite permutation graph containing every bipartite permutation graph on $n$ vertices as an induced subgraph, and let $u(n)$ be the minimum possible number of vertices of such a universal graph.

**Quadratic universal graph conjecture.** The minimum number of vertices in a bipartite permutation graph containing all $n$-vertex bipartite permutation graphs is

$$
\Omega(n^2).
$$

This conjecture asserts that the optimal universal bipartite permutation graph has quadratic size, matching the intended order of the known construction.
record.source_name: Bogdan Alecu, Vadim Lozin and Dmitriy Malyshev, “Critical properties of bipartite permutation graphs”, arXiv:2010.14467 (2020).

record.title: Uniform boundedness conjecture for Waring's problem over diagonal forms
record.statement:
Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$. For each positive integer-valued function $C:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$, let $P_C(k)=\sup_{l\geq 2}\{S_C(k,l)\}$, where $S_C(k,l)$ is the minimum number of variables $s$ for which the relevant equation is soluble over the set $\mathcal{T}_{C(k)l}$ by the Hardy–Littlewood method. **Uniform boundedness conjecture.** There exists a positive integer-valued function $C:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
P_C(k)<\infty.
$$

The conjecture asserts that, for a suitable choice of $C$, the number of variables required can be bounded independently of $l$ once $k$ is fixed. The paper explains that the available lower bound for $\lvert\mathcal{T}_t\cap[1,N]\rvert$ is insufficient to prove this statement and establishes a weaker result instead.
record.source_name: Javier Pliego, “Uniform bounds in Waring's problem over some diagonal forms”, arXiv:2010.14567 (2020).

record.title: Generalized extremal permanent conjecture for C4-free bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $A_{k,6}$ denote the smallest $k$-regular bipartite graph with girth $6$, and let $2v_k$ be the number of vertices in such a graph. Let $A\in\{0,1\}^{n\times n}$ be $C_4$-free with at most $kn$ non-zero entries. **Generalized extremal permanent conjecture.** Then

$$
\operatorname{perm}(A)\leq \operatorname{perm}(A_{k,6})^{n/v_k}.
$$

This conjecture proposes that the extremal permanent is achieved by disjoint copies of the smallest $k$-regular bipartite graph of girth $6$. The source gives no resolution and presents it as a more general open problem.
record.source_name: Igor Araujo, József Balogh and Yuzhou Wang, “Maximum determinant and permanent of sparse 0-1 matrices”, arXiv:2011.01892 (2020).

record.title: Optimal destabilization conjecture for K-unstable log Fano pairs
record.statement:
Let $(X,D)$ be a log Fano pair. For a divisor $E$ over $X$, let $A_{X,D}(E)$ denote its log discrepancy and let $S_{X,D}(E)$ denote its expected vanishing order. The stability threshold is

$$
\delta(X,D):=\inf_E \frac{A_{X,D}(E)}{S_{X,D}(E)}.
$$

**Optimal destabilization conjecture.** If $(X,D)$ is a K-unstable log Fano pair, then there exists a divisor $E$ over $X$ computing the infimum:

$$
\delta(X,D)=\frac{A_{X,D}(E)}{S_{X,D}(E)}.
$$

This asserts that the stability threshold of every K-unstable log Fano pair is attained by a divisorial valuation, providing an optimal destabilizing divisor and implying that the corresponding normalized Futaki infimum is a minimum. The supplied context does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Harold Blum, Daniel Halpern-Leistner, Yuchen Liu and Chenyang Xu, “On properness of K-moduli spaces and optimal degenerations of Fano varieties”, arXiv:2011.01895 (2021).

record.title: Albertson–Haas conjecture on planar subcubic edge-coloring
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless subcubic planar graph, meaning a planar graph of maximum degree at most $3$ with no bridges. A $(1,1,1)$-packing edge-coloring is a proper edge-coloring with three matching color classes.

**Albertson–Haas conjecture.** Every bridgeless subcubic planar graph with at least two vertices of degree $2$ admits a $(1,1,1)$-packing edge-coloring.

The conjecture is a special case of Seymour's conjecture and is described in the source as still widely open.
record.source_name: Hervé Hocquard, Dimitri Lajou and Borut Lu{ž}ar, “Between proper and strong edge-colorings of subcubic graphs”, arXiv:2011.02175 (2020).

record.title: Vanishing conjecture for the second-page spectral-sequence terms
record.statement:
Let $F$ be an infinite field and let $M_\bullet$ be the exact complex of $\operatorname{GL}_n(F)$-modules used to construct the first-quadrant spectral sequence $E^r_{p,q}(n,\mathbb Z)$ converging to zero. **Vanishing conjecture for $E^2_{i,n-i+2}(n,\mathbb Z)$.** For $n\geq3$ and every $3\leq i\leq n+2$,

$$
E^2_{i,n-i+2}(n,\mathbb Z)=0.
$$

In particular, $E^2_{1,n}(n,\mathbb Z)=0$, and the differential $d^2_{2,n}(n,\mathbb Z):E^2_{2,n}(n,\mathbb Z)\to E^2_{0,n+1}(n,\mathbb Z)$ is surjective. The statement is presented as a conjecture, and no resolution is supplied in the source.

record.title: Fujita's connectivity-preserving connected subgraph conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ and $m$ be positive integers. A graph $G$ is $k$-connected when $ba(G)\geq k$, where $ba(G)$ is the minimum size of a vertex set whose deletion disconnects $G$ or leaves only one vertex; write $b4(G)$ for the minimum degree, and let $|W|$ denote the order of a graph or subgraph $W$. **Fujita's conjecture.** There is a least non-negative integer $f_k(m)$ such that every $k$-connected graph $G$ satisfying

$$
b4(G)\geq \left\lfloor\frac{3}{2}k\right\rfloor-1+f_k(m)
$$

contains a connected subgraph $W$ of exact order $m$ such that $G-V(W)$ is still $k$-connected. Fujita and Kawarabayashi proposed this as a degree threshold for connectivity-preserving connected subgraphs; it was later confirmed by Mader, who proved $f_k(m)=m$ and that $W$ can be chosen to be a path.
record.source_name: Lian Luo, Yingzhi Tian and Liyun Wu, “Connectivity keeping paths in k-connected bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2011.03929 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.03929

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2020). “For general $k\geq2$, Conjecture 2 remains open.”

record.title: Hippchen's conjecture on intersections of longest paths
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $k$-connected graph. A **longest path** in $G$ is a path with the maximum possible number of vertices among all paths in $G$.

**Hippchen's conjecture.** Any two longest paths in $G$ share at least $k$ vertices.

The conjecture concerns how the vertex-connectivity of a graph controls intersections among its longest paths. The source reports that Gutiérrez proved it for $k\leq 4$ and for $k\geq \frac{n-2}{3}$, while the paper improves these ranges to $k=5$ and $k\geq \frac{n+2}{5}$; the parser provides no evidence that the full conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Eun-Kyung Cho, Ilkyoo Choi and Boram Park, “Improvements on Hippchen's Conjecture”, arXiv:2011.09061 (2020).

record.title: Minimum-size multipartite covering conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 2$ and $\ell\geq 1$. A **complete $k$-partite $k$-graph** is a complete $k$-partite $k$-uniform hypergraph, and $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ form a $k$-partite covering of order $\ell$ of $\binom{[n]}{k}$ when every edge of $\binom{[n]}{k}$ lies in at least one and at most $\ell$ of these hypergraphs. **Minimum-size multipartite covering conjecture.** If $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ form such a covering of minimum size, then

$$
m=\Theta\left(n^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor/\ell}\right).
$$

This covering conjecture is proposed because it would establish the sharpness of the prime-modulus oddtown conjecture. The source identifies it as a possible hypergraph extension of a result of Alon on bipartite coverings; its resolution is not given.
record.source_name: Jason O'Neill and Jacques Verstraëte, “A note on k-wise oddtown problems”, arXiv:2011.09402 (2020).

record.title: Li et al.'s neighbor product distinguishing total coloring conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with at least two vertices. The neighbor product distinguishing total chromatic number $\chi”_{\prod}(G)$ is the smallest number of colors in a neighbor product distinguishing total coloring of $G$, where the product at a vertex is the product of its color and the colors of its incident edges. **Li et al.'s conjecture.**

$$
\chi”_{\prod}(G)\leq\Delta(G)+3.
$$

This conjecture proposes a uniform upper bound in terms of the maximum degree for neighbor product distinguishing total colorings; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Aijun Dong and Wenwen Zhang, “Neighbor product distinguishing total colorings of corona of subcubic graphs”, arXiv:2011.10455 (2021).

record.title: The upper-bound conjecture for construction lines determined by registration marks
record.statement: Let $k\geq 3$ registration marks be points in the plane, and consider the construction lines determined by the arrangement, subject to the two rules in Section 1. **Upper-bound conjecture.** At most $k+1$ construction lines are determined by the $k$ registration marks. The conjecture is motivated by the classification of near-pencils, augmented near-pencils, and railtracks, all of which determine at most $k+1$ construction lines; no arrangement with more than $k+1$ lines has been identified, but the claim remains open.

record.title: The leaf-end conjecture for alternating paths in bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with matching number $
u(G)$ and saturation number $\mu(G)$ satisfying

$$
\dfrac{\mu(G)}{\nu(G)}<1.
$$

Let $M,H,H'$ satisfy the conditions that $M$ is a maximum matching and that are specified in the source. **Leaf-end conjecture.** If $G$ is bipartite, then the end-vertices of maximal $M$-$H$ alternating paths, which are also end-vertices of even maximal $H$-$H'$ alternating paths, are leaves. This conjecture would greatly restrict the possible locations of unmatched edges in bipartite graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Zhengda Mo, Sam Qunell, Anush Tserunyan and Jenna Zomback, “Characterization of saturated graphs related to pairs of disjoint matchings”, arXiv:2011.11187 (2021).

record.title: The size Ramsey number conjecture for matchings versus multiple paths
record.statement:
Let $n\ge 5$ and $m\ge 3$. For graphs $G$ and $H$, write $\hat{r}(G,H)$ for their size Ramsey number, and let $K_2$ be a single edge and $P_m$ a path on $m$ vertices. The graph $2K_2$ is the matching consisting of two disjoint edges, and $nP_m$ is the disjoint union of $n$ copies of $P_m$. **The size Ramsey number conjecture.**

$$
\hat{r}(2K_2,nP_m)=\min\{nm+1,(n+1)(m-1)\}.
$$

The preceding results establish the corresponding formula for small values of $n$, while determining the exact value for general $n$ remains open.
record.source_name: Valentino Vito and Denny Riama Silaban, “Two types of size Ramsey numbers for matchings of small order”, arXiv:2011.12065 (2021).

record.title: The unimodality-or-bimodality conjecture for restricted fractional-partition generating functions
record.statement: Let $r(x)$ be the generating function whose coefficients $f_{O_j}(k)$ count the relevant partitions into fractions with fixed denominator $j$, with $k$ ranging over the integer values considered in the paper. A coefficient sequence is **unimodal** if it increases to a maximum and then decreases, and **bimodal** if it has two modes. **Unimodality-or-bimodality conjecture.** The generating function $r(x)$ is always either unimodal or bimodal.
record.source_name: Zachary Hoelscher and Eyvindur Ari Palsson, “Counting Restricted Partitions of Integers into Fractions: Symmetry and Modes of the Generating Function and a Connection to ω(t)”, arXiv:2011.14502 (2020).

record.title: Maximum total eccentricity conjecture for graphs with fixed cut vertices
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph in $\mathfrak{C}_{n,s}$, the class used in the paper for graphs with $n$ vertices and $s$ cut vertices, and let $\varepsilon(G)$ denote its total eccentricity index. Let $U_{n,n-s}^l$ be the graph defined in the paper's preceding notation.

**Maximum total eccentricity conjecture.** For $n\geq 5$ and $2\leq s\leq n-4$, if $G\in\mathfrak{C}_{n,s}$, then

$$
\varepsilon(G)\leq\varepsilon(U_{n,n-s}^l).
$$

The preceding theorems establish the corresponding extremal result for the case $s=n-3$, while this statement proposes the same form of upper bound for the remaining range $2\leq s\leq n-4$.

record.title: Margalit's conjecture on the smallest finite non-cyclic quotient of the braid group
record.statement: Let $B_n$ be the braid group on $n$ strands, and let $\Sigma_n$ denote the finite quotient under consideration. A finite quotient is **non-cyclic** if it is not a cyclic group. **Margalit's conjecture.** For $n \geq 5$, $\Sigma_n$ is the smallest finite non-cyclic quotient of $B_n$. This conjecture concerns the problem of determining the smallest finite quotients of braid groups that are not cyclic. The preceding theorem gives a lower bound for the size of every non-cyclic finite quotient, but the conjectured minimality of $\Sigma_n$ remains unresolved here.

record.title: Convergence conjecture for substitutions in the Robba ring
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{R}$ be the Robba ring associated with a finite-height substitution $\varphi$ induced by $s(X)$, and let $\rho(s)$ be the largest norm of a zero of $s$ in the open unit disk. For $r<1$, write $\mathcal{R}^{[r;1[}$ for the subring of elements convergent on the annulus with radii $r\leqslant |z|<1$, and let $\mathcal{R}^+$ denote the positive-power subring.

**Convergence conjecture.** If $h\in\mathcal{R}$ is such that $\varphi(h)$ is convergent on the annulus

$$
\{z,\,\rho(s)\leqslant |z|<1\},
$$

then $h\in\mathcal{R}^+$.

The paper proves this conjecture in the cyclotomic case $s(X)=(1+X)^p-1$. It predicts that convergence of the substituted element on the largest forced annulus already implies that the original element has no negative powers.

record.title: Unavoidable torsion in sparse lifts conjecture
record.statement: A sparse chain complex over $\mathbb{F}_2$ has a sparse lift to integer coefficients when its boundary operators can be lifted while remaining sparse. **Torsion obstruction conjecture.** There exist sparse chain complexes over $\mathbb{F}_2$ that have a sparse lift to integer coefficients, but every sparse integer lift has some torsion in its homology and cohomology. Moreover, there exist sparse $1$-complexes with trivial homology and cohomology for which every sparse integer lift has some torsion in homology and cohomology. This would exhibit torsion as an unavoidable obstruction even when a sparse lift exists and the original complex is homologically trivial; the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Michael Freedman and Matthew B. Hastings, “Building manifolds from quantum codes”, arXiv:2012.02249 (2021).

record.title: The regularity bound for the stabilization point of the minimum distance function
record.statement:
Let $S=\mathbb{K}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $\mathbb{K}$, and let $I\subseteq S$ be a radical homogeneous ideal whose associated primes are generated by linear forms. Let $r_I$ denote the stabilization point of the minimum distance function $\delta_I$ of $I$, and let $\operatorname{reg}(S/I)$ denote the Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity of $S/I$.

**Regularity bound conjecture.** One should have

$$
r_I\leq \operatorname{reg}(S/I).
$$

The bound would extend the known inequality for ideals with $\dim(S/I)=1$ to the stated class of radical homogeneous ideals. However, the conjecture does not hold in general.
record.source_name: Luis Núñez-Betancourt, Yuriko Pitones and Rafael H. Villarreal, “Bounds for the Minimum Distance Function”, arXiv:2012.02882 (2020).

record.title: The conjecture that every 3-edge-connected graph has Frank number at most 3
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a $3$-edge-connected graph. Its **Frank number** $f(G)$ is the minimum number of orientations needed so that every edge is deletable in at least one of them. **Frank-number conjecture.** Every $3$-edge-connected graph $G$ satisfies

$$
f(G)\leq 3.
$$

The paper proves the general upper bound $f(G)\leq 7$, obtains $f(G)=3$ for the Petersen graph, and gives improved bounds for more restricted graph classes. Improving the general bound to $3$ remains open.
record.source_name: Florian Hörsch and Zoltán Szigeti, “Connectivity of orientations of 3-edge-connected graphs”, arXiv:2012.03259 (2020).

record.title: Fujita–Kawarabayashi connected-subgraph removal conjecture
record.statement:
Let $k$ and $m$ be positive integers. A graph is $k$-connected when its connectivity number is at least $k$, and $f(G)$ denotes the minimum degree of $G$.

**Fujita–Kawarabayashi conjecture.** There is a least non-negative integer $f_k(m)$ such that every $k$-connected graph $G$ satisfying

$$
f(G)\geq\left\lfloor\frac{3k}{2}\right\rfloor+f_k(m)-1
$$

contains a connected subgraph $W$ of order $m$ for which $G-V(W)$ is still $k$-connected.

The conjecture generalizes results guaranteeing the deletion of one vertex or one edge while preserving $k$-connectivity. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so the conjecture is recorded as open.
record.source_name: Meng Ji and Yaping Mao, “Note on the connectivity keeping spiders in k-connected graphs”, arXiv:2012.04816 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.04816

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2020). “The conjecture is open for $k\geq 4$ till now.”

record.title: Antunes–Freitas conjecture on three eigenvalues determining a triangle
record.statement:
Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be triangles, and write $\lambda_i(T_j)$ for their $i$th eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian. **Antunes–Freitas conjecture.** If

$$
\lambda_i(T_1)=\lambda_i(T_2),\qquad i=1,2,3,
$$

then $T_1$ and $T_2$ are identical up to a rigid motion. Antunes and Freitas supplied extensive numerical evidence for this claim, but the source reports that the first, second, and fourth eigenvalues do not uniquely determine a triangle. The conjecture itself remains open.
record.source_name: Zhiqin Lu and Julie Rowlett, “The sound of symmetry”, arXiv:2012.05851 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.05851

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: The conjecture on the number of maximum modulus curves for magic entire functions
record.statement:
Let $f$ be an entire function of the form specified in the paper, and let $\mu_f$ denote its inner degree. Write $J_f$ for the index set parametrizing the components of the maximum modulus set ${\mathcal{M}}(f)$ near the origin. The function $f$ is **magic** when $\#J_f>\mu_f$. **Magic-function cardinality conjecture.** If $f$ is magic, then

$$
\#J_f=2\mu_f.
$$

The preceding results show that magic functions have more than their inner degree of such components, while the paper leaves open the exact size of $\#J_f$. This conjecture would determine the number of disjoint curves in ${\mathcal{M}}(f)$ near the origin.
record.source_name: Vasiliki Evdoridou, Leticia Pardo-Simón and David J. Sixsmith, “On a result of Hayman concerning the maximum modulus set”, arXiv:2012.07409 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.07409

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: Main trace conjecture for genuine Picard modular forms
record.statement:
Let $\lambda\neq(0,0,0)$, let $\nu$ and $\mu$ be as in the paper, and write $\lambda=(a,b,i)$ so that $i\equiv_2 a+b$. Let $T(\nu)$ be the Hecke operator, $F_\nu$ the corresponding Frobenius, $S_{n(\lambda)}^{\rm gen}(\Gamma[\sqrt{-3}])^\mu$ the $\mu$-isotypic genuine subspace, and $e_{c,\mu}(\lambda)$ and $e_{\rm extr,\mu}(\lambda)$ the cohomological terms defined in the paper. **The main trace conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(T(\nu),S_{n(\lambda)}^{\rm gen}(\Gamma[\sqrt{-3}])^\mu\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_\nu,e_{c,\mu}(\lambda)-e_{\rm extr,\mu}(\lambda)\bigr).
$$

This is intended to compute genuine Hecke traces from point counts after subtracting Eisenstein and lift contributions; its status is explicitly conjectural in the source.
record.source_name: Jonas Bergström and Gerard van der Geer, “Picard modular forms and the cohomology of local systems on a Picard modular surface”, arXiv:2012.07673 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.07673

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: Face-lattice conjecture for partial permutohedra
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}(m,n)$ be the partial permutohedron and let $\mathcal{B}_m$ be the Boolean lattice of subsets of $[m]$. For a chain in $\mathcal{B}_m$, the difference between its largest and smallest nonempty subsets means the difference of their ranks. **Face-lattice conjecture.** Faces of $\mathcal{P}(m,n)$ are in bijection with chains in $\mathcal{B}_m$ whose difference between largest and smallest nonempty subsets is at most $n-1$. A face of $\mathcal{P}(m,n)$ has dimension $k$ if and only if the corresponding chain has $k$ missing ranks. This conjecture extends the established characterization for $\mathcal{P}(m,m)$ and proposes a corresponding description when $m\ne n$.
record.source_name: Dylan Heuer and Jessica Striker, “Partial permutation and alternating sign matrix polytopes”, arXiv:2012.09901 (2022).
record.references:

record.title: The conjecture on monophonic position numbers of cages
record.statement:
A **$(d,g)$-cage** is a graph of minimum possible order among graphs with degree $d$ and girth $g$, and ${\rm mp}(G)$ denotes the monophonic position number of $G$. **The cage monophonic position conjecture.** For sufficiently large $g$, the monophonic position number of a $(d,g)$-cage $G$ satisfies

$$
{\rm mp}(G)<d.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by the computed monophonic position numbers of the Petersen, Heawood, and McGee graphs, which are three, three, and two, respectively. It predicts that for cages of sufficiently large girth, the monophonic position number is strictly smaller than the degree.

record.title: Guan et al.'s extremal graph conjecture for Ky Fan norms of LI-matrices
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, where $n\leq m\leq 2n-3$. Let $G_{m,n}$ denote the graph referred to in the source as the candidate extremal graph, and let $||LI(G)||_{F_2}$ and $||LI(G)||_{F_3}$ be the second and third Ky Fan norms of the LI-matrix of $G$.

**Extremal graph conjecture.** Among all connected graphs with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges satisfying $n\leq m\leq 2n-3$, the graph $G_{m,n}$ is the unique graph attaining the maximum of both $||LI(G)||_{F_2}$ and $||LI(G)||_{F_3}$.

This conjecture concerns uniqueness of the extremal graph for the second and third Ky Fan norms in the range from bicyclic graphs through graphs with $2n-3$ edges. It is presented as being based on a conjecture of Guan et al.; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Zhen Lin, Lianying Miao, Guanglong Yu and Han Sheng, “On the Ky Fan k-norm of the LI-matrix of graphs”, arXiv:2012.11162 (2022).

record.title: Amaro et al.'s strengthened signless Laplacian eigenvalue-sum conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n\geq5$ vertices and $3\leq k\leq n-2$, let $Q(G)$ be its signless Laplacian matrix, and let $S_k(Q(G))$ denote the sum of its $k$ largest eigenvalues. Define $H_{n,k}$ to be the $P_3$-join graph isomorphic to $P_3[(n-k-1)K_1,K_{k-1},K_2]$. **Amaro et al.'s conjecture.**

$$
S_k(Q(G))\leq S_k(Q(H_{n,k}))<e(G)+\binom{k+1}{2},
$$

with equality if and only if $G=H_{n,k}$. This is presented as a strengthening of Ashraf et al.'s conjecture; the source records that the latter is proved in several graph classes, but does not give a resolution of this stronger claim.
record.source_name: Zhen Lin, Lianying Miao and Shuguang Guo, “On the sum of the largest A_α-eigenvalues of graphs”, arXiv:2012.11177 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.11177

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2020). “Gernert's conjecture was disproved by Nikiforov , who gave examples of graphs with $S_2(A(G))\geq \frac{29+\sqrt{329}}{42}n-25>1.122n-25$ and proved that $S_2(A(G))\leq \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}n<1.155n$.”

record.title: The A-alpha signless Laplacian eigenvalue-sum conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and $e(G)$ edges. For a real parameter $\alpha\in[0,1]$, define

$$
A_{\alpha}(G)=\alpha D(G)+(1-\alpha)A(G),
$$

where $D(G)$ is the diagonal degree matrix and $A(G)$ is the adjacency matrix; let $S_k(A_{\alpha}(G))$ be the sum of the $k$ largest eigenvalues. **The $A_{\alpha}$-eigenvalue-sum conjecture.** If $\frac12\leq\alpha<1$, then, for $1\leq k\leq n$,

$$
S_k(A_{\alpha}(G))\leq\alpha e(G)+\alpha\binom{k+1}{2}.
$$

At $\alpha=\frac12$, this would imply the corresponding signless Laplacian bound after using $2A_{1/2}(G)=Q(G)$. The supplied text does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Zhen Lin, Lianying Miao and Shuguang Guo, “On the sum of the largest A_α-eigenvalues of graphs”, arXiv:2012.11177 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.11177

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2020). “Gernert's conjecture was disproved by Nikiforov , who gave examples of graphs with $S_2(A(G))\geq \frac{29+\sqrt{329}}{42}n-25>1.122n-25$ and proved that $S_2(A(G))\leq \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}n<1.155n$.”

record.title: Dihedral commutant conjecture for dual-unitary qubit circuits
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal M'_T$ be the commutant of the algebra generated by the operators $M_a$ and $M_{ab,\iota}+R_{2t}M_{ab,\iota}R_{2t}$ on the periodic chain of $2t$ spins, where $R_{2t}$ is reflection of the time lattice and $\Pi_{2t}$ denotes translation on that chain. **Dihedral commutant conjecture.** The commutant $\mathcal M'_T$ is the linear span of the representation of the dihedral group $D_t$ on the periodic chain of $2t$ spins:

$$
\mathcal M'_T=\operatorname{span}\{R_{2t}^n\Pi_{2t}^{2\tau}:\ \tau=0,1,\ldots,t-1,\ n=0,1\}.
$$

The statement is presented without proof as the analogue of a preceding commutant characterization and would determine the infinite-system spectral form factor through $\dim\mathcal M'_T$.
record.source_name: Bruno Bertini, Pavel Kos and Tomaz Prosen, “Random Matrix Spectral Form Factor of Dual-Unitary Quantum Circuits”, arXiv:2012.12254 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.12254

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: Berge–Füredi–Meyniel conjecture on the chromatic index of linear hypergraphs
record.statement:
For a hypergraph $H$ and a vertex $v\in V(H)$, define its neighborhood by

$$
N(v):=\bigcup_{v\in e\in E(H)}(e\setminus\{v\}).
$$

Let $\Delta^*(H)$ be the maximum of $|N(v)|$ over all vertices $v\in V(H)$. A **linear hypergraph** is one in which any two distinct edges intersect in at most one vertex, and its **chromatic index** is the minimum number of colors needed to color its edges so that intersecting edges receive different colors.

**Berge–Füredi–Meyniel conjecture.** For any linear hypergraph $H$, its chromatic index is at most $\Delta^*(H)+1$.

This is presented as a generalization of the Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture. The supplied text describes it as a conjectural strengthening and does not state that it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Dong Yeap Kang, Tom Kelly, Daniela Kühn, Abhishek Methuku and Deryk Osthus, “A proof of the Erdős-Faber-Lovász conjecture”, arXiv:2101.04698 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04698

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

record.title: Oliveros et al.'s transversal-number conjecture for intersecting segment systems
record.statement:
Let $(P,\mathcal{L})$ be an intersecting $r$-segment system, where $r\geq 5$ is an integer, and let $\tau$ denote its transversal number. **Oliveros et al.'s conjecture.** Every intersecting $r$-segment system satisfies

$$
\tau\leq\lceil r/2\rceil.
$$

This conjecture concerns the maximum transversal number of intersecting segment systems and is attributed in the source to Oliveros et al.; the source gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Adrián Vázquez Ávila, “On transversal numbers of intersecting straight line systems and intersecting segment systems”, arXiv:2101.04708 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04708

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

record.title: Elphick–Wocjan eigenvalue-sum conjecture for clique number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a non-empty graph with $m$ edges, adjacency eigenvalues $mu_1\geq\cdots\geqmu_n$, clique number $omega$, and $n^+$ positive eigenvalues. Set $ell=\min(n^+,omega)$. **Elphick–Wocjan conjecture.**

$$
\mu_1^2+\mu_2^2+\cdots+\mu_\ell^2\leq\frac{2m(\omega-1)}{\omega}.
$$

The conjecture strengthens the Bollobás–Nikiforov conjecture by using up to the $omega$ largest positive eigenvalues. The paper proves it for weakly perfect, Kneser, Johnson and classes of strongly regular graphs, while the general case remains open.
record.source_name: Clive Elphick, William Linz and Pawel Wocjan, “Two conjectured strengthenings of Turán's theorem”, arXiv:2101.05229 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.05229

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2021). “Conjecture is a generalization of the conjecture proposed by Edwards and Elphick and proved by Nikiforov in .”
